Why a Home Addition?

Moving is expensive, disruptive, and often unnecessary. A well-planned home addition can give you the space you need, a new master suite, a bigger kitchen, an extra bedroom, or a full second storey, without leaving the neighbourhood where your family has roots.

Grand Design Build has delivered home additions across Toronto and the GTA since 2010. We handle the entire project under one roof: a fixed-price contract, with permits handled in-house and a dedicated coordinator running the schedule from the first site visit through to handover.

What We Build

Types of Home Additions

Not every home needs the same kind of addition. The right approach depends on your lot, your existing structure, your municipality's zoning rules, and what the addition is actually for.

Real project photo — second storey addition

Second Storey Additions

Convert a bungalow into a two-storey home. Add bedrooms, bathrooms, and a primary suite without reducing your yard space. Ideal for growing families in established Toronto neighborhoods where lots are too valuable to build out on.

Explore Second Storey Additions →
Real project photo — rear addition

Rear Addition & Main-Floor Extensions

Extend the back of your home to expand the kitchen, dining area, or living room into a larger, open-concept footprint. Popular for Toronto semi-detached and detached homes.

Explore Rear Additions →
Real project photo — side addition

Side Additions & Extensions

If your lot allows, a side addition can add a bedroom, mudroom, bathroom, or expanded entryway, often the most cost-effective way to add square footage. Works particularly well in semi-detached homes where one side is exposed.

Explore Side Additions →
Real project photo — attic conversion

Attic Conversions & Dormers

Unlock unused space above your existing ceiling. Attic conversions and dormer additions can yield a full bedroom, bathroom, and study without touching the main structure.

Explore Attic Conversions →
Real project photo — garage addition

Garage Additions & Over-Garage Suites

Build a new detached or attached garage, or add a studio suite above an existing garage. Ideal for additional living space, a home office, or rental income.

Explore Garage Additions →
Real project photo — basement extension

Basement Extension & Underpinning

Lowering and reinforcing an existing foundation to create a full-height, functional basement. We manage excavation, structural engineering, waterproofing, and interior finishing, everything.

Our Process

From Home Addition Idea to Final Move-In

 

01

Complimentary Consultation

We meet at your home, review the existing conditions, and discuss your goals, wish list, and timeline. We assess feasibility and give you an honest early read on scope and budget range.

02

Zoning & Feasibility

Our team reviews by-laws for your specific address: setbacks, height limits, lot coverage, angular plane, and FSI. We identify whether your project is as-of-right or requires a variance.

03

Design & Fixed-Price Quote

Our in-house architects develop concept drawings, and our designers walk you through finishes and materials. Once you've approved the design, we lock in your fixed-price contract.

04

Permit-Ready Drawings & Approvals

We produce full architectural and structural drawings, coordinate engineering, and manage the City of Toronto permit submission and approval process, including any Committee of Adjustment hearings.

05

Construction & Trade Management

Our on-site supervisor coordinates all trades, manages the schedule, and performs documented quality checks at each milestone. You receive regular updates from your project coordinator.

06

Final Walkthrough & Handover

We walk through every detail together, address any deficiencies on the spot, and deliver your home with full documentation; permits, warranties, and maintenance guides included.

We Handle All Of It

Permits & Approvals

Toronto's permitting and zoning process is detailed and time-sensitive. Our team manages every submission, inspection, and approval, so you don't have to.

Zoning Review

▾

We verify setbacks, height, lot coverage, FSI, angular plane, and parking requirements specific to your property and addition type.

As-of-Right vs. Minor Variance

▾

We confirm whether your project qualifies as-of-right or requires a minor variance, and represent you at the Committee of Adjustment if needed.

Architectural & Structural Drawings

▾

Our in-house architects and structural engineers produce complete, permit-ready drawing packages — no third-party coordination required.

City Permit Submission & Follow-up

▾

We submit to the City, track your application, respond to examiner comments, and push the process forward to avoid unnecessary delays.

Heritage, TRCA & Tree Coordination

▾

For properties in heritage areas, ravine-adjacent lots, or those with significant trees, we coordinate all additional approvals and protective measures.

Construction Inspections & Closeout

▾

We schedule and manage all required City inspections throughout construction and obtain final occupancy sign-off when the project is complete.

Do I Need a Permit for My Addition?

Yes, all home additions in Toronto require a building permit. The process varies depending on whether your project is as-of-right under current zoning or requires additional approvals.

Many projects are straightforward and receive permits without hearings. Others require a minor variance application, a process we manage completely on your behalf, including representation at the Committee of Adjustment.

The short answer: don't worry about it. We've guided over 250 addition projects through Toronto's approvals process. Your coordinator will explain exactly what's needed for your specific project from day one.

Questions

FAQs

Yes, all home additions require a building permit. Many projects are as-of-right, meaning they comply with existing zoning rules and can be permitted without additional hearings. If your project exceeds lot coverage, setbacks, height limits, or FSI limits, a minor variance application is required. Grand Design Build manages the entire permit and approval process, including Committee of Adjustment representation when needed.

The timeline varies by project type. A rear main-floor addition typically takes 4–6 months from permit approval to handover. A full second-storey addition on a bungalow typically runs 7–10 months. Design and permitting add 2–4 months before construction begins. Your project coordinator will give you a specific schedule before you sign your contract, and milestones are tracked throughout.

It depends on your lot and goals. Second-storey additions maximize square footage without reducing yard space, ideal for smaller lots. Rear additions are often simpler structurally and less disruptive to live in during construction. Many homeowners combine both. We'll review your property and zoning during the initial consultation and recommend the option that gives you the best outcome for your budget.

In most cases, yes, though there will be periods of disruption, particularly when structural work is underway or when the roof is open during a second storey build. We plan phasing to minimize disruption and give you advance notice of the most intensive periods.

The terms are used interchangeably. Both refer to adding new square footage to an existing home by building outward (rear or side extension) or upward (second storey addition).

Three things: we're HCRA licensed (required for this type of structural work in Ontario), we offer fixed-price contracts (your quote is your price), and we back every addition with a 7-year structural guarantee. Most contractors offer none of these. We offer all three.
